name: Median of the live orders
brief:
A venue shows the median size of its live orders, and orders arrive and are cancelled. The input comes as one string.

The first line holds `q`, the number of events.

Each of the next `q` lines is `+ x`, a new order of size `x`, or `- x`, the cancelling of one live order of size `x`. A cancelled size is always live.

After each event, record the lower median of the live sizes: with `m` live orders sorted, the one in place `(m + 1) // 2`, counting from 1. Record `-` when nothing is live.

Write `solve_live_median(text)`, which returns the records separated by single spaces. Expect extra spaces and a trailing newline.

Example. For `"4\n+ 5\n+ 1\n- 5\n- 1\n"` the live sizes are {5}, {1, 5}, {1} and none. The answer is `"5 1 1 -"`.
constraints: $0 \le q \le 400{,}000$ events; sizes are whole numbers from 1 to $10^9$, and equal sizes may be live at once.
$O(q \log q)$ time is the target. Sorting the live sizes after every event is far too slow, and a sorted list with insertions in the middle is $O(q^2)$ moves.
All the tests in a run share one 5-second limit in the browser.
hint: Keep the lower half in a max-heap and the upper half in a min-heap, with counts of how many live orders each holds. Cancel lazily: note the size against its half, and pop noted sizes only when they reach the top. Rebalance after every event so the lower half holds `(m + 1) // 2`.

examples.note: With 1 and 5 live the lower median is 1, the first of the two.
Two orders of size 3 are live at once; cancelling one leaves the other.

tests.call:
(lambda out: (len(out), out.count('-'), sum(int(t) for t in out if t != '-'), out[-3:]))(solve_live_median('400000
' + '
'.join('+ %d' % (i * 7919 % 1000003 + 1) if i < 300000 else '- %d' % ((i - 300000) * 3 * 7919 % 1000003 + 1) for i in range(400000)) + '
').split())

(lambda out: (len(out), out.count('-'), sum(int(t) for t in out if t != '-'), out[-3:]))(solve_live_median('200000
' + '
'.join('- %d' % ((i - 2) * 37 % 1000 + 1) if i % 3 == 2 else '+ %d' % (i * 37 % 1000 + 1) for i in range(200000)) + '
').split())

how: Submit runs 12 hidden tests. Each answer must equal the expected value. The obvious method sorts the live sizes after every event, or keeps them in a sorted list, which runs out of time on the large tests. The step to the target is two heaps split at the median, with cancellations noted and removed lazily when they reach a top.
notes: The lower half's top is the lower median as long as that half holds `(m + 1) // 2` live orders.
A cancelled order stays in its heap until it reaches the top, so the sizes of the halves must be counted, not read from the heaps.
Each order is pushed and popped a bounded number of times, so the work is $O(q \log q)$.

planted.slip: Reading the lower top without clearing cancelled sizes off it first can report an order that is gone.
One shared record of cancelled sizes lets a cancel in one half remove an equal live order from the other.
Splitting each line on a single space breaks on the extra spaces the input may carry.
A sorted list shifts every later size on each insert and cancel, so the large test runs far past the limit.
